inconsistencies: Soft-fork cluster: #35793 (BIP 54), #31989 (CTV), #32247 (CSFS), #29247 (OP_CAT) and #36122 (CISA) are all non-mainnet, flag- or regtest-gated consensus implementations; they were spread across P1-P3 individually. Banded together at P2 (#36122 stays P3 as an explicit not-for-merge draft vendoring unmerged libsecp256k1).
Chain: #35793 must land before #35861 (Testnet 5 is based on it and awaits BIP 54 merge). Review #35793 first.
Chain: #32575 is the stated prerequisite for #29491 (Schnorr batch verification). Review #32575 first; #29491 additionally waits on secp256k1 #1134/#1789.
Chain: #35646 unblocks #35570 (it is what lets validation methods return BlockValidationState). Review #35646 first.
Chain: #35731 is built on top of #35714. Review #35714 first; #35731 adds little on its own.

Overlapping approaches to the same problem: #29700, #35003, #35646, #35714, #35731, #36049 and #34132 all rework fatal/IO error propagation out of block storage and validation. #35003 carries an open Approach NACK on collapsing exceptions into nullable returns; that architectural decision governs the others, so it should be settled before the cleanup PRs in the cluster are polished.

Assumeutxo cluster: #36346, #35307, #36452, #36542, #36500, #36543 and #35054 all touch snapshot loading/background validation. #36346 and #35307 fix the same failure mode (crash leaving a node needing -reindex); #36452 and #36542 both fix startup aborts. Review them adjacently to avoid conflicting fixes to the same code paths.

Stateless-validation cluster toward #35904: #35906, #36066, #35569 and (via the kernel) #35187 are steps of one program; #35906 is the one with concrete test-coverage payoff, the others are preparatory.
#35195 and #34864 both change coins-cache internals (hasher traits vs. entry-state flags) and will likely conflict; #35751 and #36496 both build on the CoinsViewOverlay from merged #35295.
#35271 addresses a condition observed only in a downstream fork (Elements) and reviewers doubt Core is affected; it may be closeable rather than reviewable.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: a small P1 set of reachable crash/data-loss bugs (witness-DoS, assumeutxo crashes, reindex data destruction, block-index corruption), a broad P2 band of chainstate-integrity fixes, measured IBD/block-connection performance, and the regtest soft-fork implementations, then a long P3 tail of error-handling and coins/blockindex refactors. The main correction made across the list was levelling the proposed-soft-fork implementations into one band and lifting bug fixes whose symptom is a failed startup or silent corruption above feature and refactor work.
